speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with yellowish discoloration of the skin; have you noticed this jaundice is spreading to your stomach or legs, or is it only on your face and chest? Also, has your baby been feeding well and how many wet diapers have you changed in the last day?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia (likely Breastfeeding Jaundice).

Given the jaundice is spreading from the face to the trunk on day 5, I need to know if your baby has passed meconium and if it has turned to yellow/brown stool, as this is crucial for assessing bilirubin excretion. Please also confirm if the baby is having at least 6 wet diapers per day.
